question_type: balance-sheet share (a row group over a total) at six dates, mean per set of three dates, absolute difference in percentage points; the CPI deflator cancels inside each same-date share
decisive_step: Which asset rows of Table ESF-1 form 'foreign-exchange holdings and securities': the two currency rows (European euro, Japanese yen) that follow the label-only header 'Foreign exchange and securities:', excluding the 'Accounts receivable' line printed after them and excluding U.S. Government securities and SDRs. Secondary decisions that all cells got right: dates are columns of the lagged quarterly issues (June 30 = closing column of the December issue, Sept. 30 = closing column of the March issue, each reprinted as the opening column of the next issue, identical); 'average share' = mean of the three per-date shares, under which the CPI factor multiplies numerator and denominator of each share and cancels. Reference: worklog Step 3 ('Foreign exchange and securities has no subtotal row -> FX&S = euro + yen'), Step 4 footing check (the five asset rows add to Total assets), Step 6 reading A; solution.structured key_decisions.

smallest_change.change: show_table: stop dropping label-only rows, and print the row footing. In otables.py the segment builder (around lines 1164-1180) consumes every 'section' row as a segment boundary and `continue`s, so the CELLS (--long) view never shows it, while the ROWS view prints '== <header>' and then every data row up to the next header (so 'Accounts receivable' and 'Total assets' land under 'Foreign exchange and securities'). Change: (1) in the CELLS view emit the header as its own line, e.g. `  5232 p1 - 'Foreign exchange and securities:' [group header, no values]`; (2) in the ROWS view print the '==' line as `== Foreign exchange and securities:  (group header at line 5232; no subtotal row; flattened text keeps no indentation, so membership of the rows below is not marked)` and print total rows with a `total` flag rather than inside the group; (3) add a NOTES line computed by the existing identity checker across rows: `- row identity: 'Total assets' (5236) = U.S. Government securities + Special drawing rights + European euro + Japanese yen + Accounts receivable (5 rows, holds in all 3 columns)`. b2 would have seen the header above the two currency rows and would not have taken government securities and SDRs as 'securities'; b and c would have seen that the receivable is one of five separately listed asset lines that foot to the total, the same evidence the reference used, instead of a tool-drawn segment that appears to contain it.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: a already read the raw lines and made the same call; one extra line per header row and one NOTES line

notes: show_table's two views give opposite impressions of the same table: --long hides the group header entirely (b2 never learned it exists), while ROWS/--stitch draws a '==' segment that runs until the next header and so visually includes both the receivable and 'Total assets' (b[15]). Neither view prints the footing of the asset rows to the total, which is the check the reference used. Other friction worth fixing in v10: printings --row cannot match OCR-split labels ('To tal as sets'; a[23], c[44]-[48]): normalise labels by deleting intra-word spaces before matching; printings has no --all although find_tables does (a[8], c[16]); when --row is given a date on a table whose dates are columns, the 'no matching row/column' message should say 'periods are columns here: use --col "June 30, 2000" --row <label>' (a[10], c[17]); printings on a label-column table takes ~1 s per call and cells issued 18-30 calls in loops (a[57], b2[36], c[53]), so a --rows/--cols multi-cell form (or printing the whole row group in one call) would replace the loops. All four cells spent 10-25 steps confirming that no CPI-U index table exists in the corpus; the reference spent one grep. b's --alt behaviour (submit the primary, attach the other reading, treat the echoed Offer as a hint) is the pilot-1 lesson and should stay fixed in v10 controls.
